catalog_quote: En el plano fonológico, esta variedad consta de un pie trocaico moraico cuyo núcleo tiene como correlatos fonéticos la duración y la intensidad tal y como lo confirma el análisis estadístico. En ese sentido, hay una preferencia por ubicar a la prominencia métrica en la primera mora del pie (Kager, 1999, p. 172). ... Una de las características del sistema acentual es su carácter culminativo, puesto que sólo hay un pico prosódico por palabra fonológica en la lengua. Por otro lado, el acento también es demarcativo ya que el núcleo del pie trocaico moraico siempre tiene lugar en el linde izquierdo de la palabra mínima. [pp.312-313] ... la estructura métrica tiene un contorno fuerte-débil que ubica al núcleo en la primera mora tanto en palabras aisladas como en los demás dominios morfológicos. [p.192-193] ... (15) a. ('kuµʃiµ) kuʃi 'comer' b. ('koµoµ) koo 'serpiente' c. ('siµβiµ)teµ siβi=te 'él toca' d. ('laµaµ)ʃiµndaµ laa=ʃi=nda 'su pájaro de ustedes' ... g. nĩµ('kiµðeµ) nĩ=kiðe 'hice' h. siµ('kaµβaµ) si=kaβa 'naranja' ... Los casos de (15a-h) muestra una regularidad evidente: el pie se mantiene dentro de la palabra mínima y el núcleo se alinea al linde izquierdo. [p.205]
world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: Southern Puebla Mixtec (sout3001) is not in the catalog. The single works with stress in the title, Rueda Chaves 2019 (COLMEX doctoral thesis on the San Jerónimo Xayacatlán variety, open on the Colmex repository), was already held by the project with a text at and was re-opened at pp.191-193, 204-205 and 311-313 (PDF 215-217, 228-229, 335-337). It is a first-hand acoustic and phonological study: stress falls on the first mora of the bimoraic root/couplet (moraic trochee, ALL-FT-LEFT), is culminative and demarcative, clitics and prefixes are outside the foot (nĩ('kiðe), si('kaβa)), correlates are duration and intensity, F0 is tonal. This gives a clean 'initial (root-initial) stress' coding for a language with no catalog record. Vázquez Peralta 1997 'Gramática popular de la lengua mixteca del sur de Puebla' remains unlocated (per). A search note was appended to in the save directory.

new_statements.translation: Phonologically, this variety has a moraic trochaic foot whose head has duration and intensity as its phonetic correlates, as the statistical analysis confirms. In that sense there is a preference for placing metrical prominence on the first mora of the foot (Kager 1999: 172). [...] One characteristic of the stress system is its culminative character, since there is only one prosodic peak per phonological word in the language. Stress is also demarcative, since the head of the moraic trochee always falls at the left edge of the minimal word [= the bimoraic root couplet].

new_statements.rule_in_words: One primary stress per phonological word, on the first mora (first syllable) of the bimoraic root couplet (CVCV, CVV etc.), i.e. root-/couplet-initial; the foot is a moraic trochee left-aligned in the minimal word; proclitics/prefixes and enclitics are not footed and never stressed (('siβi)=te 'he plays', nĩ=('kiðe) 'I did', si=('kaβa) 'orange'), so position in the full word is fixed by where the couplet begins. Correlates are duration (strongest) and intensity; F0 belongs to the three level tones and is only raised on the tonic; tone never relocates stress in this variety (contrast Ayutla Mixtec).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not a separate lexical category; compounds of two couplets foot both, primary on the first ((ˈˈndutʃi)(ˈnũũ) 'ojo', p.205), and in utterances trochaic feet alternate left-to-right, one peak per couplet, avoiding stress clash (p.206-207, ex. 18).
new_statements.exceptions: None lexical. Bimoraic monosyllables (CVV) carry stress on the first mora; clitic moras outside the couplet are unparsed (PARSE-SYL, NONFINALITY dominated by ALL-FT-LEFT); stressed syllables show raised F0 for all three level tones (tone depends on stress, PROMTONEMATCH), whereas in Ayutla Mixtec (not this language) high tone attracts stress. Lit. review notes phrase-level stress on the last pre-pausal syllable reported for Acatlán Mixtec by Pike & Wistrand 1974.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain of stress = the minimal word / bimoraic couplet (root); statement holds 'tanto en palabras aisladas como en los demás dominios morfológicos' (p.192-193), i.e. citation forms, cliticised noun phrases and verb forms; based on ~2018 elicited isolated items (3 repetitions, 2 speakers) plus phrases and paradigms, with t-tests/Wilcoxon/LDA on duration, intensity, F0.
new_statements.identity_note: Rueda Chaves 2019 describes the Mixtec of the municipio of San Jerónimo Xayacatlán (SJX), centre-south Puebla, which the author places in the Mixteca Baja / Josserand's Northern Baja dialect area and calls 'un dialecto afín al mixteco de Acatlán (Pike y Wistrand, 1974)' (p.8). Glottolog files the thesis under sout3001 Southern Puebla Mixtec (ISO mit; Ethnologue's 'Acatlán area' Mixtec). Data: 2 elderly L1 speakers (F 88, M 79), ~2018 elicited lexical items x3 repetitions plus phrases/paradigms. The related Méndez-Hord 2017 UND thesis treats the neighbouring town Xayacatlán de Bravo ('Acatlán Mixtec'), same glottocode; Pike & Wistrand 1974 treat Acatlán (de Osorio) Mixtec, also mit.

new_statements.quote: (i) la palabra mínima del mixteco es un pie bimoraico; y (ii) el pie tiene un patrón fuerte débil, es decir, es un pie trocaico. [...] la estructura métrica tiene un contorno fuerte-débil que ubica al núcleo en la primera mora tanto en palabras aisladas como en los demás dominios morfológicos. [p.313:] Una de las características del sistema acentual es su carácter culminativo, puesto que sólo hay un pico prosódico por palabra fonológica en la lengua. [...] el acento también es demarcativo ya que el núcleo del pie trocaico moraico siempre tiene lugar en el linde izquierdo de la palabra mínima.
new_statements.translation: (i) the Mixtec minimal word is a bimoraic foot; and (ii) the foot has a strong-weak pattern, i.e. it is a trochee. [...] the metric structure has a strong-weak contour that places the head on the first mora, both in isolated words and in the other morphological domains. [p.313:] One characteristic of the stress system is its culminative character, since there is only one prosodic peak per phonological word in the language. [...] stress is also demarcative, since the head of the moraic trochee always falls at the left edge of the minimal word.
new_statements.citation: Rueda Chaves, John Edinson (2019). La interacción entre el tono y el acento en el mixteco de San Jerónimo de Xayacatlán. Tesis de doctorado, El Colegio de México. 332 pp.
new_statements.locator: §4.1.2 pp.192-193 (PDF 216-217), generalizations (3) and following paragraph; §6.2.1 p.313 (PDF 337)
new_statements.reading: Fixed initial stress on the bimoraic root (couplet): the first mora / first syllable of the (C)V(C)V or (C)VV root bears stress (moraic trochee, left-aligned); one stress per phonological word; affixes and clitics attached to the root are unstressed (foot head stays at the root's left edge, so with proclitics the stress is root-initial rather than word-initial, e.g. nĩ('kiðe), si('kaβa)); compounds have one foot per root. Correlates: duration and intensity; F0 belongs to tone (three level tones B/M/A, mora as TBU). Consistent with the general Mixtecan couplet-initial trochee.

sources.note: Per Méndez-Hord 2017 (pp.2, 15, 47, 62): reanalyses Acatlán Mixtec in Register Tier Theory - underlyingly toneless TBUs surface with a default Lo tone (pp.101-102); Pike & Wistrand's 'step-up terrace tone' is analysed as upstep, a floating Hi (register feature h) raising all subsequent Hi tones to extra-high (pp.105-115); an OCP-type condition on adjacent H is attributed to Snider for Acatlán.
